phrase: reports the enemy's doings to Eteocles
note: Eteocles, mighty prince of the Cadmeans, I have returned with a sure report; Eteocles acts on it

phrase: slaughter a bull over a shield
note: slaughtered a bull over a black shield; part of the oath ritual

phrase: swear to sack the city or die
note: they swore an oath ... that either they will level the city ... or will in death smear this soil with their blood; the assault follows
on Adrastus' chariot they were placing remembrances of themselves for their parents at home
and were shedding tears while so doing; taken as a distinct act within the event
I left them casting lots to decide how each commander ... would lead his regiment against the gates; each later stands at his gate by lot

phrase: advances on the city in armour
note: the Argive army in full armor is advancing in a flurry of dust

phrase: urges Eteocles to man the gates fast
note: choose the bravest men of the city and station them quickly at the outlets of the gates; Eteocles later posts champions
I, on my part, will keep a reliable eye on the lookout ... [Exit.]; he returns later with his gate-by-gate report

phrase: prays the gods not to destroy the city
note: O Zeus and Earth, and gods that guard our city, and Curse ... do not destroy my city; the city is saved; the Curse (Erinys) is also addressed
[Exit Eteocles, with citizens.
The Chorus enters in fearful agitation.]; Eteocles later rebukes their panic

phrase: charges out of camp at the city
note: Leaving camp, —look!—the mounted throng floods swiftly ahead; drives the chorus to the statues
shall I fall in supplication at the feet of our ancestral gods' statues? ... the time has come to hold fast to your statues; Eteocles rebukes this

phrase: begs the gods to save the city
note: Oh come all you gods who guard our city ... See this suppliant band of maidens praying to be saved from slavery; Eteocles answers it
The Argives encircle the citadel of Cadmus

phrase: take their stand at the seven gates
note: Seven bold captains ... at the seven gates take their stand each according to his lot; the scout reports each one

A hail of stones strikes our battlements from afar ... the clang of bronze-bound shields at the gates; the chorus later gives this as why it fled to the statues; the clanging is not taken as a separate act

phrase: rebukes the chorus for spreading panic
note: You intolerable things! ... your cries ... have rattled the citizens into dispirited cowardice; the chorus answers him

phrase: threatens disobeyers with death by stoning
note: if anyone fails to obey my authority ... a sentence of death will be decreed for him ... destruction by stoning; a decree for a future case, written as a threat
Keep inside and do no harm!; not obeyed

phrase: tells the chorus to be silent
note: Be silent, wretched woman; do not terrify your own men.; answered by the promise
I am silent. I will suffer what is destined together with the others.; answers his command

phrase: tells the chorus to pray calmly
note: keep your distance from the gods' images and make a stronger prayer ... without your previous lamentation; the chorus heeds him and prays

phrase: vows sacrifices and spoils to the gods
note: I vow that, if things go well and the city is saved, the citizens shall redden the gods' altars ... and offer trophies; never fulfilled in the play

phrase: says he will post seven champions
note: I will go station six men, with me as the seventh, as champions; he does post them
[Exit.]
against our fortifications some are advancing with all their men; the assault later fails
Others are hurling jagged boulders at the citizens on all sides

phrase: prays the gods to strike the attackers
note: divine guardians of the city, hurl murderous destruction on the men outside our walls and panic
[The Scout is seen approaching from one side; brings the gate report
Eteocles from the other.]; "here is our lord himself ... at the right moment to hear the messenger's report"

phrase: reports who stands at each gate
note: I will give my account of the enemy's actions, how each man according to lot has been posted at the gates; Eteocles answers each in turn
Tydeus is already storming opposite the Proetid gates; Melanippus is sent against him

phrase: keeps Tydeus from crossing the river
note: the seer will not allow him to ford the Ismenus because the omens from the sacrifices are not favorable
lashes skilled Oecles' son, with the taunt that he cringes in cowardice before death and battle
against Tydeus I will station the trusty son of Astacus as defender of this gate; six gates hold
[Exit Melanippus.]
May the gods grant success to our champion

phrase: boasts he will destroy the city despite Zeus
note: he says he will utterly destroy the city with god's will or without it, and that not even conflict with Zeus ... will stand in his way; Eteocles and the chorus answer it
against him ... mighty Polyphontes, is stationed
[Exit Polyphontes.]

phrase: calls death by thunderbolt on Capaneus
note: Death to him who exults so arrogantly over the city! May the thunderbolt stop him

phrase: draws the third lot, the Neistan gate
note: The third lot leaped out of the upturned bronze helmet for Eteoclus, to hurl his band against the Neistan gates

phrase: boasts not even Ares could throw him off
note: shouts in syllables of written letters that even Ares could not hurl him from the battlements; Megareus is sent in answer
I would send this man here ... Megareus, Creon's seed
[Exit Megareus.] Indeed, he has already been sent

phrase: prays for Megareus and against the boasters
note: I pray that this man will have good fortune ... may Zeus the Requiter look on them in anger!

phrase: takes his stand at Onca Athena's gate
note: Another, the fourth, has the gate near Onca Athena and takes his stand; Hyperbius is set against him
takes his stand with a shout ... The warrior himself has raised the war-cry
Hyperbius, Oenops' trusty son, is chosen to match him, man to man
[Exit Hyperbius.]

phrase: swears by his spear to sack the city
note: He swears by his spear ... that he will sack the city of the Cadmeans in spite of Zeus; Actor is sent in answer
There is a man for this one, too ... Actor, brother of him I named before
[Exit Actor.]

phrase: prays the gods destroy the boasters
note: May the gods destroy them here in our land!
he repeatedly rebukes mighty Tydeus with evil names Murderer, maker of unrest in the city

phrase: rebukes Polynices for attacking his homeland
note: he addressed your own brother ... Will such a deed as this be pleasing to the gods ... that you sacked the city of your ancestors

phrase: brought a foreign army against his city
note: launched a foreign army against them; the whole war and the herald's decree rest on it

phrase: foretells his own burial in enemy soil
note: I will enrich this earth, a seer interred beneath enemy soil
I will station a man against him, mighty Lasthenes
[Exit Lasthenes.]
May Zeus strike them with his thunderbolt outside the walls and slay them!

phrase: prays to take the city and kill Eteocles
note: His prayer is that after he mounts the battlements and is proclaimed king ... once he kills you, that he may perish at your side ... invokes his native gods; Eteocles goes to meet him and both die
in the same way as you dishonored him with exile; the cause of Polynices' attack

phrase: bears a shield where Justice promises his return
note: She claims to be Justice ... I will bring this man back and he will have his city; the act is Polynices bearing the device; Eteocles answers it
our father's curses are brought to fulfillment; "he launched brutal, wrathful words against the sons he had bred"; the brothers die by it
I will go and stand against him—I myself in person; leads to the mutual killing
Quick, bring my greaves to protect against spears and stones!; asked of unnamed attendants

phrase: begs Eteocles not to fight his brother
note: No, son of Oedipus ... do not be like in temperament to him; "Do not yourself take the road to the seventh gate!"; answered by his refusal

phrase: dreamt the division of the father's wealth
note: Too true were the phantoms in my sleeping visions, predicting the division of our father's wealth!; a thing undergone more than done

phrase: will not be turned from his purpose
note: you will not blunt my sharpened purpose with words; answers the chorus
When it is the gods who give you evils, you cannot flee them. [Exit.]; he dies there
Apollo who ... said three times that the king would save his city if he died without offspring; Laius' defiance answers it
he, overcome by the thoughtlessness of his longing, fathered his own death, the parricide Oedipus
the parricide Oedipus; "With the hand that killed his father"
who sowed his mother's sacred field ... Madness united the frenzied bridal pair; the sons are born of it

phrase: rids the land of the plague
note: when he removed that deadly, man-seizing plague from our land
the thronging assembly of men ever admired so much as they honored Oedipus; the gods are named alongside the men

phrase: learns the truth of his marriage
note: when, his sanity regained, he grew miserable in his wretched marriage; leads to the blinding and the curse
he struck out his eyes, which were dearer to him than his children
Take heart, you daughters ... Our city has escaped the yoke of slavery
we have fortified the gates with champions ... all is well, at six of the gates; the city is saved; champions named as citizens

phrase: takes the seventh gate for himself
note: lord Apollo ... took for himself the seventh gate, accomplishing upon the children of Oedipus the ancient follies of Laius
The men are dead, murdered by their very own hands; "did they each kill the other together?"; mourning and decree follow
through their mutual murder the earth has drunk the blood of the two kings
[The funeral procession with the bodies of the brothers comes into view.]; bearers unnamed, given as citizens
here come Antigone and Ismene to do their bitter duty, the dirge over their brothers both

phrase: bore the brothers to her own son
note: After she made her own child her own husband, she gave birth to these sons
they did much to harm our citizens and also the ranks of all the foreigners who died in abundance; the foreigners are the Argive army
Antigone standing by the bier of Polynices; "Ah, the grief, brother all-lamentable"
Ismene by that of Eteocles; "Ah I pity your grievous suffering, my king"

phrase: decrees honour for Eteocles, no burial for Polynices
note: Such is the decree of the Cadmean authorities; "this corpse of Polyneices is to be cast out of the city unburied"
It is my duty to announce the will and decrees of the council on behalf of the people; Antigone answers it

phrase: says she will bury Polynices anyway
note: I will bury him alone ... Nor am I ashamed to act in defiant opposition to the rulers of the city
I forbid you to act thus in violation of the city.
I will bury him. Put an end to your big talk.
but I forbid it
Well then, follow your own rash plan ... [Exit.]

phrase: goes with Antigone to bury Polynices
note: We, at all events, will go and bury him with her, following the funeral procession; closes the action; First Half-Chorus
We will go with this other corpse ... [Exeunt omnes.]; closes the action; Second Half-Chorus
Dionysus, whom once Semele, Kadmos' daughter, bore, delivered by a lightning-bearing flame
having taken a mortal form instead of a god's; the disguise lets him deceive Pentheus
I, the son of Zeus, have come to this land of the Thebans
the tomb of my thunder-stricken mother ... smouldering with the still living flame of Zeus' fire; the sisters' slander and the tomb fire rest on it

phrase: brought about the insult to Semele
note: the everlasting insult of Hera against my mother; what Hera did is not spelled out
I praise Kadmos, who has made this place hallowed, the shrine of his daughter
I have covered it all around with the cluster-bearing leaf of the vine

phrase: passed through the lands of Asia
note: I have left the wealthy lands of the Lydians ... and all of Asia

phrase: set up his dances and rites there
note: having already set those other lands to dance and established my mysteries there; his Asian band comes from there
I have first excited Thebes to my cry, fitting a fawn-skin to my body and taking a thyrsos in my hand

phrase: said Dionysus was not Zeus' son
note: my mother's sisters ... claimed that I, Dionysus, was not the child of Zeus ... they boasted that Zeus killed her; the cause of their madness

phrase: drove his aunts mad to the mountains
note: Therefore I have goaded them from the house in frenzy, and they dwell in the mountains; leads to the killing

phrase: made them wear his rites' dress
note: I have compelled them to wear the outfit of my mysteries

phrase: drove all Theban women mad from home
note: all the female offspring of Thebes ... I have driven maddened from the house; Pentheus hurries back over it
Now Kadmos has given his honor and power to Pentheus, his daughter's son
who fights against the gods as far as I am concerned; the god's vengeance answers it
drives me away from sacrifices

phrase: leaves him out of his prayers
note: in his prayers makes no mention of me, for which I will show him

phrase: vows to show Thebes he is a god
note: I will show him and all the Thebans that I was born a god

phrase: threatens war if Thebes attacks the Bacchae
note: if ever the city of Thebes should in anger seek to drive the the Bacchae down from the mountains with arms, I ... will join battle with them; undergoer taken as Pentheus for the city
you women who have left Tmolus ... whom I have brought from among the barbarians as assistants and companions

phrase: orders the chorus to drum round the palace
note: going about this palace of Pentheus beat them, so that Kadmos' city may see
I myself will go to the folds of Kithairon, where the Bacchae are, to share in their dances
From the land of Asia, having left sacred Tmolus, I am swift to perform for Bromius
For I will celebrate Dionysus with hymns according to eternal custom

phrase: casts the unborn child from her womb
note: the thunder of Zeus flying upon her, his mother cast from her womb, leaving life by the stroke of a thunderbolt; the striking is ev 3

phrase: hides the child in his thigh
note: having covered him in his thigh shut him up with golden clasps, hidden from Hera

phrase: brings him forth as a horned god
note: he brought forth, when the Fates had perfected him, the bull-horned god
he crowned him with crowns of snakes
the Korybantes ... invented for me in their caves this circle, covered with stretched hide
handed it over to mother Rhea
raving Satyrs ... joined it to the dances of the biennial festivals

phrase: agreed to dress for the god
note: what agreement I, an old man, have made with him ... to twine the thyrsoi, to wear fawn-skins; both appear so dressed
He knows why I have come

phrase: calls Kadmos out of the house
note: Call from the house Kadmos, son of Agenor

phrase: comes out dressed for the rites
note: I have come prepared with this equipment of the god; Pentheus mocks this dress

phrase: take each other's hands to go
note: come, take hold of my hand. / "Here, take hold, and join your hand with mine."

phrase: heard of the women's new rites
note: I happened to be at a distance ... when I heard ... that the women have left our homes in contrived Bacchic rites
is coming here to the house now in haste

phrase: had some of the women caught
note: As many of them as I have caught; they are later set free

phrase: keep the women bound in prison
note: servants keep in the public strongholds with their hands bound

phrase: threatens to hunt and chain his aunts
note: as many as are absent I will hunt from the mountains, I mean Ino and Agave ... and Autonoe ... having bound them in iron fetters

phrase: mocks the two old men's dress
note: I see Teiresias the soothsayer in dappled fawn-skins and my mother's father—a great absurdity; Teiresias and Kadmos answer him

phrase: snatched the infant from the lightning
note: when Zeus snatched him out of the lighting-flame
and led the child as a god to Olympus

phrase: wanted to cast him out of the sky
note: Hera wished to banish him from the sky; only intended

phrase: gave Hera a piece of air as hostage
note: Having broken a part of the air ... he gave this to Hera as a pledge

phrase: urges Pentheus to receive the god
note: Receive the god into your land, pour libations to him; Pentheus answers with orders against him

phrase: will not be made to fight the god
note: I will not be persuaded by your words to fight against the god

phrase: urges Pentheus to call Dionysus a god
note: Even if, as you say, he is not a god, call him one; and tell a glorious falsehood

phrase: boasted he hunted better than Artemis
note: having boasted that he was superior in the hunt to Artemis
who was torn apart in the meadows by the blood-thirsty hounds he had raised; the hounds are not in the cast

phrase: offers to crown Pentheus with ivy
note: Come, let me crown your head with ivy
Don't lay a hand on me!
Let someone go quickly to the seat where he watches the flights of birds, upset and overturn it ... release his garlands to the winds

phrase: orders the stranger hunted and bound
note: some of you hunt throughout the city for this effeminate stranger ... bring him here bound; the servants catch him

phrase: goes off with Kadmos to pray
note: Let us go, Kadmos, and entreat the god, on behalf of him; Kadmos later returns from the Bacchae with him

phrase: warns Kadmos of trouble from Pentheus
note: Beware lest Pentheus bring trouble to your house, Kadmos; it comes true, but nothing hangs on the warning
Pentheus, we are here, having caught this prey for which you sent us
laughed and allowed us to bind him and lead him away
we are here, having caught this prey; the questioning follows

phrase: get free of the public prison
note: are set loose and gone ... the chains were loosed from their feet and keys opened the doors without human hand; no human doer named
Release his hands
First then tell me who your family is.

phrase: says he is a Lydian sent by Dionysus
note: Lydia is my fatherland ... "Dionysus, the child of Zeus, sent me"; the disguise holds until the end
You must pay the penalty for your evil contrivances.; answered at once
And you for your ignorance and impiety toward the god.; carried out later

phrase: threatens to cut the stranger's hair
note: First I will cut off your delicate hair.
Next give me this thyrsos from your hands.

phrase: orders the stranger seized and bound
note: Seize him; he insults me and Thebes! ... "I ... bid them to bind you."

phrase: warns Pentheus not to bind him
note: I warn you not to bind me, since I am in my senses and you are not.

phrase: has the stranger shut by the stables
note: Shut him up near the horse stable, so that he may see only darkness.; he escapes from there

phrase: threatens to sell or enslave the chorus
note: we will either sell them or ... I will keep them as slaves at the loom
I will go, for I need not suffer that which is not necessary.

phrase: warns that Dionysus will pursue Pentheus
note: Dionysus, who you claim does not exist, will pursue you for these insults

phrase: received the infant in her streams
note: venerable Dirce ... you once received the child of Zeus in your streams
when Zeus his father snatched him up from the immortal fire
and saved him in his thigh, crying out: Go, Dithyrambus, enter this my male womb
Go, Dithyrambus ... so that they will call you by this name

phrase: calls Dionysus down to check Pentheus
note: Come, lord, down from Olympus ... and restrain the insolence of the blood-thirsty man; he answers from within
[within] Io! Hear my voice, hear it, Io Bacchae
Io! Io! Master, master! Come now to our company, Bromius.

phrase: shakes Pentheus' palace with an earthquake
note: Shake the world's plain, lady Earthquake! ... "Did you see these stone lintels on the pillars falling apart?"; leads to Pentheus' confusion

phrase: sets fire blazing round Semele's tomb
note: Light the fiery lamp of lightning! ... "the fire ... about the sacred tomb of Semele"; Pentheus thinks the house burns
Cast on the ground your trembling bodies, Maenads; Dionysus raises them
[Enter Dionysus]

phrase: tells the chorus to rise and take heart
note: But get up and take courage, putting a stop to your trembling.
By myself I saved myself easily, without trouble.; Pentheus finds him escaped

phrase: shackles a bull, thinking it the stranger
note: He found a bull by the stable ... and threw shackles around its knees and hooves
thinking that the house was burning, he ran here and there, calling to the slaves to bring water

phrase: makes a phantom in the courtyard
note: Bromius ... created a phantom in the courtyard

phrase: stabs the air at the phantom
note: Pentheus rushed at it headlong, stabbing at the shining air, as though slaughtering me

phrase: knocks Pentheus' house to the ground
note: Bacchus inflicted other damage on him: he knocked his house to the ground
From fatigue, dropping his sword, he is exhausted.

phrase: slips out of the house to the chorus
note: Now I have quietly left the house and come to you; Pentheus finds him outside
[Enter Pentheus]
Ah! Here is the man ... How do you appear in front of my house, having come out?

phrase: orders the towers round about closed
note: I order you to close up all the towers around.
I have come from Kithairon

phrase: promises the herdsman he may speak freely
note: Speak, as you will have immunity from me in any case.; the report follows

phrase: wakes the sleeping Bacchae with a cry
note: Your mother raised a cry, standing up in the midst of the Bacchae, to wake their bodies from sleep
casting off refreshing sleep from their eyes, sprang upright
secured their fawn-skins ... girding the dappled hides with serpents licking their jaws
holding in their arms a gazelle or wild wolf-pup, gave them white milk
They put on garlands of ivy, and oak, and flowering yew.

phrase: strike rock and ground with thyrsoi
note: One took her thyrsos and struck it against a rock ... Another let her thyrsos strike the ground

phrase: sends forth water, wine, milk and honey
note: there the god sent forth a fountain of wine; the women later wash at these fountains

phrase: urges the herdsmen to catch Agave
note: Some one, a wanderer about the city ... said to us all: ... do you wish to hunt Pentheus' mother Agave out; the speaker is not in the cast
lay down in ambush, hiding ourselves in the foliage of bushes
I sprang forth, wanting to snatch her, abandoning the ambush

phrase: calls her Bacchae to follow her
note: O my fleet hounds, we are hunted by these men; but follow me!
We fled and escaped from being torn apart by the Bacchae
they, with unarmed hands, sprang on the heifers ... others tore apart cows

phrase: fall on and plunder two villages
note: falling like soldiers upon Hysiae and Erythrae ... they turned everything upside down; the villagers arm against them
They were snatching children from their homes

phrase: take up arms against the women
note: Some people in rage took up arms ... For their pointed spears drew no blood
the women, hurling the thyrsoi from their hands, kept wounding them
and turned them to flight

phrase: go back to the god's fountains
note: they returned where they had come from, to the very fountains which the god had sent forth
and washed off the blood
snakes cleaned the drops from the women's cheeks with their tongues; the snakes are not in the cast

phrase: urges Pentheus to receive the god
note: Receive this god then, whoever he is, into this city, master.

phrase: orders his troops to gather to attack
note: Go to the Electran gates, bid all the shield-bearers ... to assemble ... so that we can make an assault against the Bacchae; Dionysus answers it

phrase: warns Pentheus not to fight a god
note: it is not right for you to raise arms against a god, but to remain calm

phrase: threatens the stranger with prison again
note: Or shall I bring punishment upon you again?

phrase: vows to slaughter the women on Kithairon
note: I will sacrifice, making a great slaughter of the women, as they deserve, in the glens of Kithairon.

phrase: foretells the army's flight from the women
note: You will all flee. And it will be a source of shame that you turn your bronze shields away

phrase: offers to bring the women back unarmed
note: Without weapons I will bring the women here.
Alas! You are contriving this as a trick against me.
[To a servant] Bring me my armor.; the stranger's temptation cuts in

phrase: tempts Pentheus to see the women
note: Ah! Do you wish to see them sitting together in the mountains?
Lead me as quickly as possible.

phrase: talks Pentheus into women's dress to spy
note: Put linen clothes on your body then. ... "True. We must go first and spy."

phrase: goes indoors with the stranger, undecided
note: I will go in. For either I will go bearing arms, or I will obey your counsels.
Women, the man is caught in our net.

phrase: calls the god to drive Pentheus mad
note: Dionysus, now it is your job ... First drive him out of his wits, send upon him a dizzying madness; Pentheus comes out deranged
now I will go to fit on Pentheus the dress he will wear to the house of Hades

phrase: comes out dressed as a maenad
note: [Pentheus emerges.] In appearance you are like one of Kadmos' daughters.

phrase: sees two suns and the stranger as a bull
note: I think I see two suns ... you have certainly now become a bull
But I who ought to wait on you will re-arrange it. Hold up your head.

phrase: shows how to hold the thyrsos
note: You must hold it in your right hand and raise your right foot in unison with it.
Could I carry on my shoulders the glens of Kithairon, Bacchae and all?

phrase: decides to hide in the pines
note: The women are not to be taken by force; I will hide in the pines.; he is set in a pine
Follow me. I am your saving guide

phrase: says he will come back in his mother's arms
note: You will return here being carried— ... In the arms of your mother.

phrase: calls Agave and her sisters to reach out
note: Reach out your hands, Agave, and you too, her sisters ... I lead this young man to a great contest

phrase: sends Madness to drive the sisters at the spy
note: Go to the mountain, go, fleet hounds of Madness ... and drive them raving against the mad spy

phrase: calls for justice to slay Pentheus
note: Let manifest justice go forth ... slaying through the throat this godless ... offspring of Echion

phrase: calls Bacchus to snare the hunter
note: Go, Bacchus, with smiling face throw a deadly noose around the hunter of the Bacchae
Oh house once fortunate in Hellas ... how I groan for you
Pentheus, the child of Echion, is dead.; the chorus rejoices
Lord Bacchus, truly you appear to be a great god.; the messenger rebukes it
Do you rejoice at the misfortunes of my master, woman?
we began to ascend the heights of Kithairon, Pentheus and I ... and the stranger who was our guide

phrase: sit hidden in a valley near the maenads
note: First we sat in a grassy vale, keeping our feet and voices quiet, so that we might see them without being seen; he cannot see, so asks for the pine

phrase: bends a tall pine to the ground
note: seizing hold of the lofty top-most branch of the pine tree, he pulled it down ... to the dark earth
He sat Pentheus down on the pine branch
and let it go upright through his hands steadily; he is seen by the maenads
the stranger was no longer anywhere to be seen

phrase: orders the maenads to punish Pentheus
note: a voice, Dionysus as I guess, cried out from the air: ... Now punish him!; they attack

phrase: sets a holy fire between sky and earth
note: a light of holy fire was placed between heaven and earth; who placed it is not said

phrase: rush through the glen at the god's call
note: they rushed forth, swift as a dove ... his mother Agave, and her sisters, and all the Bacchae

phrase: pelt Pentheus with rocks, branches, thyrsoi
note: began to hurl at him boulders ... other women hurled their thyrsoi through the air at Pentheus ... But they did not reach him

phrase: try to tear up the tree's roots
note: began to tear up the roots of the tree with ironless levers; their failure brings Agave's order

phrase: tells the women to circle the pine
note: Come, standing round in a circle, each seize a branch, Maenads

phrase: drag the pine from the earth
note: They applied countless hands to the pine and dragged it up from the earth.
Pentheus fell crashing to the ground from his lofty seat
He threw the headband from his head so that the wretched Agave might recognize and not kill him.

phrase: begs his mother not to kill him
note: Pity me, mother, and do not kill me, your child; it fails
Seizing his left arm at the elbow ... she tore out his shoulder
Ino began to work on the other side, tearing his flesh, while Autonoe and the whole crowd of the Bacchae pressed on
The whole band ... were playing a game of catch with Pentheus' flesh. His body lies in different places; Kadmos must gather it

phrase: fixes Pentheus' head on her thyrsos
note: His miserable head ... she fixed on the end of a thyrsos

phrase: carries the head toward the city
note: and carries through the midst of Kithairon like that of a savage lion ... She is coming inside these walls

phrase: leaves her sisters on the mountain
note: leaving her sisters among the Maenads' dances
Let us honor Bacchus with the dance ... Kadmean Bacchae, you have accomplished a glorious victory
I am bringing home from the mountain a freshly cut tendril ... I caught this young wild lion cub
The honor is mine first ... His other offspring took hold of this beast after me

phrase: invites the chorus to the feast
note: Share in the feast then.
What? I share in the feast, wretched woman?

phrase: calls the citizens to see her prey
note: You who dwell in this fair-towered city ... come to see this prey; the citizens are not in this cast

phrase: calls for Kadmos and Pentheus to hang the head

on the next went to my mother and father and questioned them; one act on both parents

phrase: were angry at the drunken man
note: They were angry at the one who had let this taunt fly; the text gives a feeling, not a deed; the rumor still spread and he went anyway

phrase: foretold incest and killing his father
note: that I was fated to defile my mother's bed ... and that I would slay the father that sired me; makes him flee, and comes true

phrase: hit Oedipus's head with his goad
note: from his carriage, brought his double goad straight down on my head; Oedipus strikes back

phrase: knocked Laius out of the carriage
note: with one swift blow from the staff in this hand he rolled right out of the carriage onto his back; leads to the killing

phrase: asks Iocasta to fetch the herdsman
note: send someone to fetch the peasant, and do not neglect this matter; the herdsman is brought

phrase: prays Zeus to uphold the oracles
note: Zeus all ruling, may it not escape you and your deathless power!; nothing turns on it
with this wreathed branch and these gifts of incense in my hands ... to you, Lycean Apollo ... I have come as a suppliant; nothing turns on it
that you may find us some escape from uncleanliness; the Messenger's arrival is not presented as its answer
[Enter a messenger.]; brings the news that unravels Oedipus's birth

phrase: resolve to make Oedipus their king
note: The people will make him king of the Isthmian land, as it was said there; intended, not done; it is why the Messenger comes

phrase: sends a handmaid to fetch Oedipus
note: Handmaid, away with all speed, and tell this to your master!; Oedipus comes out

phrase: says Polybus died of old age
note: A light tilt of the scale brings the aged to their rest ... and of the long years that he had lived; leads Oedipus to scorn the oracles
Polybus has swept them with him to his rest in Hades. They are worth nothing; overturned when all comes true

phrase: reveals Polybus was not his father
note: Because you had no blood in common with Polybus; starts the search for his birth

phrase: gave the infant to the messenger
note: Another shepherd gave you to me ... one of the household of Laius; leads to the herdsman's summons

phrase: begs Oedipus to stop the search
note: For the gods' sake, if you have any care for your own life, do not continue this search!; Oedipus refuses
I will not hear of not discovering the whole truth; leads to the herdsman's questioning
[She rushes into the palace.]; she hangs herself inside
I recognize those who bring him, I think, as servants of mine / "[The herdsman is brought in.]"; leads to his questioning

phrase: tells the messenger to be silent
note: Damn you! Be silent once and for all!; Oedipus turns on him
He speaks without knowledge, but is busy to no purpose; leads to the threat
You will not speak with good grace, but will in pain; the herdsman gives in
Someone, quick—tie his hands him this instant!; the herdsman gives in

phrase: admits giving the messenger the child
note: I did. Would that I had perished that day!; leads to the question of whose child

phrase: reveals the child was Laius's own
note: it was said to be his own child. But your lady within could say best; Oedipus understands

phrase: sees the oracles have come true
note: Oh, oh! All brought to pass, all true; leads to his rushing in and blinding himself
[He rushes into the palace.]; finds Iocasta dead
[A second messenger enters from the house.]; brings the report of what happened inside

phrase: slams the chamber doors behind her
note: she dashed the doors together behind her; Oedipus must force them

note: she had given birth to a twofold brood, husband by husband, children by her child; the sons are not in the cast; the daughters are brought out at the end

asking where he could find the wife who was no wife, but a mother; no one answers
he sprang at the double doors, forced the bending bolts from the sockets; lets him reach her
and rushed into the room; he finds her

he released the halter by which she hung; nothing later depends on it except her lying there
when the hapless woman was stretched out on the ground; passive; done by Oedipus as the event says

phrase: tears the brooches from her robe
note: he tore from her raiment the golden brooches; used to blind himself

phrase: strikes his eyes again and again
note: lifting them struck his own eye-balls ... he struck his eyes with raised hand not once but often; makes him blind, as foretold

phrase: begs the elders to lead him
note: Hurry, friends, lead me from the land, lead me from here; they do not

phrase: curses the man who saved him

phrase: tells servants to take Oedipus in
note: Take him into the house as quickly as you can; not at once done

phrase: begs Creon to cast him out
note: Cast me out of this land with all speed; Creon puts it off

phrase: refuses until he asks the god
note: This I could have done ... except I craved first to learn from the god all my duty; answers the plea
give to the woman within such burial as you wish; no answer given

phrase: begs Creon to keep his daughters
note: My two girls, poor hapless ones ... I implore you to take care of them; he presses it again (ev 110)
allow me to touch them with my hands; the daughters are brought in

phrase: begs Creon to promise their protection
note: do not allow them to wander poor and unwed ... Promise, noble man, and touch them with your hand; Creon gives no answer

[Enter a band of Elders, guardians of the Persian Empire]; opens the play's action

we whom Xerxes, our King, Darius’ royal son, himself selected, by virtue of our rank and years, to be the guardians of his realm; their standing as counsellors is why Atossa turns to them and why they receive Xerxes at the end

phrase: goes forth from Susa against Hellas
note: who left behind them the walled defence of Susa and Agbatana and Cissa’s ancient ramparts, and went forth; the king goes with them ("together with the captain of the host", S013); the whole disaster follows from this

by crossing the Hellespont ... on a bridge of boats made fast with cables, thereby casting a tightly constructed roadway as a yoke upon the neck of the sea; Darius later condemns this yoking and Xerxes returns by the same bridge
[Enter Atossa, richly dressed, on a chariot and attended by a numerous retinue]; brings her to the council
I bow low before her ... "[The elders prostrate themselves and then rise to their feet]"

phrase: dreams of two women and Xerxes

phrase: yokes both women to his car
note: He yoked them both to his car and placed the collar-straps upon their necks; an act inside the dream; the women are not in the cast

phrase: stands by his son in pity
note: his father Darius stood by his side filled with pity; in the dream

phrase: advise her to pray and pour

So well as to have destroyed Darius’ great and courageous host; Atossa later says Xerxes sought "to exact retribution for them" (S066)

phrase: bids him tell the whole loss
note: relate the sum of our disaster and speak out! Who is there that is not dead?; answered by the messenger's report

phrase: batter the ships on every side
note: and battered them on every side. The hulls of our vessels rolled over

phrase: hack the men in the water
note: as if our men were tuna or some haul of fish, the foe kept striking and hacking them with broken oars and fragments of wrecked ships

it ventured to pass across the ice-bound stream

note: The survivors, after making their way through Thrace with great hardship ... escaped to the safety of the land of their homes; Xerxes among them, who later arrives

cease, noble woman, venerable partner of my bed, from your tears and laments, speak to me with all frankness

phrase: tells him the host is ruined
note: near Athens our whole host has been brought to ruin ... "Impetuous Xerxes, depopulating the whole surface of the continent"

phrase: warns them never to invade Hellas
note: If you do not take the field against the Hellenes’ land, even if the forces of the Medes outnumber theirs

phrase: tells of troops left in Boeotia

phrase: bids Atossa clothe and comfort Xerxes
note: withdraw to the palace and bring from there clothing which is suitable for him ... Soothe him with words of kindness; she leaves to do so

phrase: vows not to forsake her son
note: for I will not forsake him whom I love so well in his affliction
when I have brought appropriate garments from the palace, I will make attempt to meet my son ... [Exit]; answers Darius' bidding

phrase: held the islands under his sway
note: And he held under his sway the sea-girt islands midway between the continents

whereat I was enraged and smote his Cyclopes, forgers of the heavenly fire

phrase: forces Apollo to serve a mortal
note: so my sire in recompense for this forced me to become a slave in a mortal’s home

and kept a stranger’s flocks, and to this day have been the saviour of this house; his bond with Admetus leads to the bargain with the Fates
him I saved from death by cheating Destiny

phrase: asks his father to die instead

phrase: asks his mother to die instead
note: made trial of each, his father and the aged mother that bare him

phrase: accuses Apollo of wronging the dead

note: such a hero shall there come to Pheres’ halls, by Eurystheus sent ... will wrest this woman from thee by sheer force; fulfilled by Heracles

phrase: says he will take her below
note: that woman shall to Hades’ halls go down, I tell thee

she washed her fair white skin with water from the stream

standing before the altar-hearth, she prayed, Mistress mine ... be mother to my orphans, and to my boy unite a loving bride

and prayed, plucking from myrtle boughs their foliage

phrase: takes her children in her arms
note: she took them each in turn in her arms
and kissed them fondly, as a dying mother might

but she held out her hand to each
nor was there one so mean but she gave him a word and took his answer back

phrase: begs her not to leave him
note: and prays her not to leave him, impossible request!

note: Look, look! she cometh even now, her husband with her, from the house; Admetus comes with her; brings her death before the people

phrase: begs her not to leave him
note: Steel not thy heart to leave me, I implore, by heaven, by thy babes whom thou wilt make orphans; she answers with her request
do not marry a new wife to be a stepmother to these children ... Then do not this, I do beseech thee; he promises
no Thessalian maid shall ever take thy place and call me lord; tested when Heracles brings the veiled woman

phrase: promises to mourn her for life
note: No year-long mourning will I keep for thee, but all my life through, lady

note: I will put an end to revelry, to social gatherings o’er the wine, forego the festal crown and music which once reigned in my halls

phrase: begs her to take him below
note: Take me, O take me, I beseech, with thee ’neath the earth

I thy tender chick, printing my kisses on thy lips

phrase: bids the chorus sing to Hades
note: stay here with me and to that inexorable god in Hades raise your antiphone

note: to all Thessalians in my realm I do proclaim a general mourning for this lady ... till twelve full moons are past; his closing proclamation of dances replaces it
[[Exeunt ADMETUS and EUMELUS, with the other children.]; the children go with him

say, shall I find Admetus in the house?; Admetus comes out to him

if I with Ares’ own-begotten sons must fight, first with Lycaon
next with Cycnus

Hail! son of Zeus, from Perseus sprung; Heracles returns the greeting

phrase: calls the dead woman a stranger
note: A stranger, yet in another sense related to my house ... "Her father dead, she lived here as an orphan"; Heracles stays and revels unknowing, and later rebukes him for it

note: even now my servants are bearing the corpse with all its trappings shoulder-high to the funeral pyre; Heracles goes to the tomb

phrase: comes with gifts for the dead
note: I see thy father advancing with aged step, and servants too bearing in their arms adornment for thy wife

phrase: offers the gifts to his son
note: Accept this garniture, and let it go beneath the earth; refused

phrase: swears never to bury his father
note: For I will never bury thee with hand of mine

note: Nay, sir guest, ’tis Admetus’ wife that is no more; leads Heracles to the tomb

[[Exeunt HERACLES and Servant.]

заслонками закрыли, колодами завалили, замазали и засмолили

phrase: run off with towel, brush, comb
note: пустились бежать, взяли с собою шитую ширинку, щётку и гребёнку
а злодейка выдралась
увидала их и посвистывает: — Гай, гай, гай
Бросили щётку — вырос тростник густой-густой
Ведьма распустила когти, прощипала дорожку

phrase: throw the comb, raising a forest
note: Бросили гребёнку — выросла дуброва тёмная-тёмная

phrase: gnaws and tears a way through
note: Ведьма наострила зубы ... что ни хватит, то дерево с корнем вон!

phrase: throw the towel, raising fiery sea
note: Бросили ширинку златошвейную — разлилось море широкое, глубокое, огненное

phrase: falls into the fire and burns
note: поднялась ведьма высоко, хотела перелететь, пала в огонь и сгорела; ends the pursuit
Вот подошёл к ним человек, спрашивает: кто они?

phrase: tells his master about his sister
note: одна из них должна быть ваша сестрица, а которая — угадать нельзя
Пошёл барин поглядеть, зазвал их к себе

phrase: will not say which she is
note: она сердита — не скажется; makes the trick needed
Налью я бараний пузырь крови, положите его себе под мышку ... а я подойду и хвачу вас ножом в бок
слуга хватил барина в бок, кровь брызнула; stabs the bladder under his arm
брат упал
сестра кинулась обнимать его, и плачет, и причитывает; she reveals herself
А брат вскочил ни горелый, ни болелый
обнял сестру

phrase: marries her to a good man
note: и отдал её за хорошего человека; closes the story
а сам женился на её подруге, которой и перстенёк пришелся по ручке; answers the ring's condition

phrase: complains he can find no bride
note: Что, — говорит, — я по себе невесты не найду?
У меня есть дочка хороша; так хороша, что человек ни вздумает, то она узнает!; opens the action
написал письмо и скричал своим господам жандармам ... «Убирайся венчаться»
залилась слезами и стала убираться, и служанка с нею

performer: the merchant's daughter and her maid
note: обе на одно лицо. Вот убрались они в одинакое платье; lets the maid pass for her

performer: the merchant's daughter and her maid
note: и едут к царю венчаться
Пойдём, по острову погуляем!

phrase: drugs her with a sleeping potion
note: усыпила служанка купеческую дочь сонным зельем
вырезала у ней глаза и положила в карманчик; the eyes are later returned
Уходилась на море моя служанка
Нам лишь бы ты была жива, а эта крестьянка вовсе не нужна!
Приехали к царю; сейчас стали венчаться
Должно быть, купец меня обманул! Это не купеческая дочь; a thought, not acted on
опомнилась от болезни ... ничего она не видит, а только слышит

phrase: asks the old man for shelter
note: Прими и меня с собою
Старичок принял её

phrase: has him drive the cattle off
note: Дедушка, отгони скотину-то! Он её послушал — отогнал скотину

phrase: sends him for cloth on credit
note: Возьми ты бархату и шёлку в долг
Из богатых никто не дал в долг, а дали ему из бедной лавки
Дедушка, ложись спать и ухом не веди
стала из бархату и шёлку царскую корону шить
Поди, отнеси к царю; ничего не проси, а проси только глаз
Тут все над этой короной сдивовались
а тот и с него глаз просит
царь заругался и хотел уж его в острог сажать; only intended

phrase: orders a captive's eye cut out
note: Подите, у пленного солдата вырежьте глаз!; overtaken by the tsaritsa
царица, сейчас выскочила, вынимает глаз и даёт его царю
Ах, как ты меня выручила, царевнушка!

phrase: gives the old man the eye
note: и отдал старику этот глаз
пришёл в свою избушку ... — Взял
вышла на зорю, поплевала на глазок, приставила — и стала видеть

phrase: sends him to pay and buy
note: велела долг отдать за шёлк и за бархат и ещё приказала взять бархату и золота
Вот она села шить другую корону

phrase: sends him to request an eye
note: Ничего не бери, только глаз проси; а станут тебя спрашивать ... скажи: мне бог дал!
Дай мне глаз, — просит старик
а супруга царева тут же и вынимает другой глазок

phrase: asks where he gets the crowns
note: Где ты, старичок, берёшь эти короны?
Мне бог дал!
Приходит в избушку, отдаёт глазок слепенькой
поплевала глазок, приставила его — и стала видеть обоими глазами

phrase: finds herself in a glass house
note: а то вдруг очутилась в стеклянном дому; no one is said to do it
и завела она гулянья; draws the tsar
Едет царь посмотреть, что такое за диво
сейчас его принимает и за столик сажает
зовет её к себе в гости

phrase: praises the girl to his wife
note: какой в этом месте дом и какая в нем девица! Кто что ни вздумает, то она узнает!
Это, верно, она, которой я глаза вырезала!

phrase: visits her again and invites her
note: царь опять едет к ней в гости ... и зовет её в гости

phrase: gives him a bottomless money chest
note: Вот тебе сундук денег: до дна его не добирай — всегда будет полон

phrase: tells him to bury her pieces
note: убьют и в мелкие части изрубят; ты встань поутру, сделай гробок, собери мои кусочки и похорони
жандармы приехали, посадили её и повезли
а царица на неё и не смотрит — сейчас застрелила бы её

phrase: orders the girl cut to pieces
note: иссеките её в мясные части и выньте у ней сердце да привезите ко мне!

phrase: tells them to cut her quickly
note: Секите ж меня скорее!
Они иссекли её, вынули у ней сердце

phrase: bury her in a dung heap
note: а самою в назём закопали

phrase: take her heart to the tsaritsa
note: и приехали во дворец. Царица вышла, взяла сердце

phrase: rolls the heart into an egg
note: скатала его в яйцо и положила в карман; the boy later takes the egg

phrase: wakes in his hut and weeps
note: встал в избушке и залился слезами
Сделал гроб
нашел в навозе, разрыл, собрал все части, положил их в гроб и похоронил у себя; a garden grows on the grave
едет к купеческой дочери в гости

phrase: finds a garden on her grave
note: где она схоронена, там над ней сад вырос
Ездил-ездил, не нашёл ни дома, ни девицы, а только один сад!
Ступайте вы, посеките на том месте сад!

phrase: try to cut the garden down
note: стали его сечь, а он весь окаменел
хочется сад посмотреть; вот и едет глядеть его
увидал в нём мальчика — и какой хорошенький мальчик!
Взял его во дворец
так раскричался, что ничем его и не забавят
Царица вынула из карманчика яичко, скатанное из сердца, и дала ему; the heart returns to the girl
Мальчик побёг на двор ... он в сад
а царь за ним ... и царь в сад
Увидал там этот царь девицу и очень обрадовался
Я твоя невеста, купеческая дочь, а царица твоя — моя служанка

phrase: begs her forgiveness on her knees
note: Царица упала ей в ноги: — Прости меня!

phrase: reminds her she showed no mercy
note: А ты меня не прощала: один раз глаза вырезала
Жандармы! Вырежьте же теперь и царице глаза и пустите её в поля

phrase: blind her, tie her to horses
note: Вырезали ей глаза, привязали к коням и пустили в поля. Размыкали её кони по чистому полю

performer: the tsar and his young tsaritsa
note: А царь с младой царицею стали жить да поживать; closes the story

phrase: takes to flying into the garden
note: змий черноморский и повадился туда летать
змий черноморский и унёс их на своих огненных крыльях; opens the action

phrase: sends maids to search the garden
note: Послал служанок искать их в саду

phrase: search but do not find them
note: служанки не нашли царевен
Утром царь сделал тревогу, народу собралось множество

phrase: promises money to whoever finds them
note: Кто разыщет моих дочерей, тому сколько угодно дам денег; answered by the treasury at the end

performer: a drunken soldier, Frolka the Sitter and Yeryoma
note: Вот и избрались трое: солдат-пьяница, Фролка-сидень и Ерёма
уговорились с царём
и пустились искать царевен
сильный сон стал одолевать их; not a person's act
пхнул в нос охапку табаку

phrase: rouses the others to go on
note: Эй, братцы, не уснём, не воздремлем! Идите дальше
приходят, наконец, к огромному дому, а дом этот был пятиглавого змия
стукнул в двери так сильно, что расшиб их

phrase: warns the dragon will eat them
note: Ведь здесь живёт прелихой змий; он вас съест!

phrase: boasts they will eat the dragon
note: Мы сами его съедим!
вот и летит змий, летит и рычит: — Кто моё царство разорил?
Ворон меня не занесёт ... а добрый конь завезёт!
Не мириться я пришёл ... а драться!
Фролка с одного маху срубил все пять голов змию

phrase: hides the heads, buries the body
note: положил их под камень, а туловище зарыл в землю
Возьмите меня, голубчики, с собою
Царевна позвала их в хоромы, накормила-напоила

phrase: begs them to free her sisters
note: и просит, чтоб они выручили и других её сестер
Да мы за этим и посланы!

phrase: tells where her sisters are held
note: Царевна рассказала, где живут её сестры
Приходят к средней сестре
Фролка что ни есть силы бухнул в ворота, и ворота растворились
Вдруг летит семиглавый змий
сразился с змием и с одного маху сшиб ему все семь глав
положил их под камень, а туловище зарыл в землю
в четвёртой увидали среднюю царскую дочь
она повеселела, начала угощать их

phrase: begs them to save her sister
note: просила выручить от двенадцатиглавого змия её меньшую сестру
рычали так громко ... товарищи его от страха попадали на землю
а товарищи его от страха попадали на землю

phrase: stays standing and leads them on
note: пойдёмте за мною! — и пошли дальше
в этих палатах живёт двенадцатиглавый змий
Когда так ... ступайте; я проведу вас туда
Старик подошёл ко львам и начал их гладить
тут Фролка пробрался с своими товарищами на двор

phrase: takes them to the youngest princess
note: старик повёл их в ту комнату, где жила царевна
Царевна угостила их
а сама уж начала сряжаться
вдруг видят в версте от них летит змий ... Змий сначала очень шибко напал на них
Тут царская дочь бросилась назад в хоромы
а Фролка с товарищами пошёл навстречу и сразился с змием
успел одержать победу, сшиб ему все двенадцать голов
и кинул их в овраг
начали гулять от радости пуще прежнего
зашли за другими царевнами
и все вместе прибыли на родину
растворил им свою царскую казну ... берите, сколько угодно, себе денег за работу; keeps his promise
Фролка первый стал насыпать, сыпал-сыпал, треуха и прорвалась, и серебро утонуло в грязь
Ерёма давай-ка, пока деньги есть, насыпать лукошко, а солдат ранец
насыпали и пошли себе домой
А Фролка с треухою остался подле царской казны и поныне сидит да насыпает; closes the story
унадився вяликий зверь — Норка яго звали — и багата рабив шкоды: каждаю ночь поедав зверей; opens the action
Хто истребить Норку-зверя, дам тому палавину царства
як только наступила ночь, ён взяв аружие и пашов

phrase: drinks all night in a tavern
note: зайшов у трактир и там прагуляв целаю ночь; fails, so the youngest goes
На другий день и средний брат зрабив такжа
батько лаяв-лаяв их, да и перестав
Смеялись все з яго, бо був дурный
узявши аружия, пашов прямо у зверинец да и сев над дерном, штоб ... яны его кальнули

phrase: leaps the fence into the menagerie
note: Норка-зверь бяжить и пряма через аграду в зверинец
пашов прямо на зверя
ён назад, царевич за им
пабег в канюшню, узяв самага лучшага жеребца
дагнав таго зверя да и давай бицца
Царевич дав зверю три раны; the sister later says she healed them
выбились из мочи да и лягли аддыхать
Як только царевич заснув, зверь устав да й наутёки
Конь будя царевича

phrase: twice more overtakes and wounds it
note: Царевич и тут зрабив зверю три раны ... знова зрабив три раны
лягли аддыхать. Зверь утёк

phrase: lifts the white stone and descends
note: зверь дабег да великага белага камня, падняв яго и пашов на той свет
Тогда мяне пабедиш, як сюда придеш; a challenge the tsarevich takes up
расказав аццу свайму все

phrase: asks for a long leather rope
note: прасив яго, штоб ён вялев звить кожаный канат такий довгий
Атец вялев

phrase: takes his brothers to the stone
note: забравши сваих братов, набравши слуг ... паехав туда, где зверь пашов пад камень

phrase: build a palace and live there
note: яны пастроили там дварец и стали жить
Ни адин и з места не двинув
а ён як хватив, дак камень далеко палятев
А хто пайдя на тей свет ... Не адин не взявсь
насмеявшись над ими, што яны трусы
апускайтя мяне на той свет ... и як толька закалышицца канат — тащитя

phrase: lower him into the other world
note: Браты апустили яго
А, здрастуй, Иван-царевич; долга я дожидав табе!
Ён сев на таго коня и паехав
глядить, аж стаить медный дварец
Там нагатована абедать; ён сев, паабедав
пашов у спальню; там пастель, и ён лег аддыхать
Хто в моем доме — азавися
Ён вышов

phrase: rejoices and names him her husband
note: взрадавалась ... Иван-царевич (муж мой ты будешь любезный); she follows him later
Ён расказав ёй, што и як

phrase: says the beast is her brother
note: Той зверь, што ты хочеш пабедить, — мой брат ... я яму залячила три раны
яны пили, гуляли, добры мысли мали
паехав да другой сястры, што в серебряном дварце, и в той также пагастив

phrase: says Norka is at the youngest's
note: Яна сказала яму, што брат яё Норка тяперь у меньшай сястры

phrase: says Norka sleeps on the sea
note: брат яё тяперь спит на синём море

phrase: gives strong water and a sword
note: дала яму напицца сильнай вады, дала меч-кладенец
сказала, штоб ён рубав главу брату адразу

phrase: finds Norka asleep on a stone
note: аж спить Норка на камне, пасерядине моря
ударив мечем па галаве. Галава адскачила ... и павалився у море

phrase: takes all three sisters with him
note: пабрав всех трех сястер с сабою ... бо все яго любили
Кажная из их из свайго дварца зрабила яичко
яго научили, як из яичка зрабить дварец, и наабарот
аддали яму яички; used for the dresses later
царевич, пасадив девушек, дерганув за канат
браты патащили. Як вытащили
Пустим канат, падымем брата, канат перярежим, нехай убьецца
брат быв не промах, дагадався, што братья думають
узяв да и палажив камень, дерганув
братья падняли его высоко да и перярезали канат. Той камень упав и разбився; meant to kill him; leaves him below
Ён заплакав да и пашов
пришов к деряву, штоб захавацца пад ним

phrase: covers the fledglings with his clothes
note: ён изняв с сабе адёжу да и накрыв их; earns the bird's help
Ета ты зрабив? Спасиба табе
Чаго хочеш, праси ад мяне за ета; все сделаю для табе!
Выняси мяне на тей свет

phrase: tells him to fill a bin
note: Зраби ж ты вяликий засек, налави всякай дичи ... налий вады
Царевич все зрабив
взятши етат засек на сабе ... вынясла яго

phrase: takes her leave and flies away
note: папращалась и палятела
пристав к аднаму партному у хлопцы: такий он быв абодранный, так перемянився
хочуть, штоб им к вянцу нашить всякага платья, такога, як у них было на том свете, и без мерки ... не адин не бярецца

phrase: sends the tailor to the tsar
note: Иди, хазяин, к царю и скажи, што ты нашиеш все ... Я отвечаю за всё
дав яму денег, сколько ён хатев
выняв из кармана тыя яички ... зделав из их три дварцы
вашов, пабрав у каждом их платья

phrase: turns the palaces back into eggs
note: звярнув тые дварцы в яички

phrase: hangs the dresses up at home
note: развешав платья на стяне да и лег спать

phrase: takes the dresses to the tsar
note: взяв панёс тоя платья к царю
дагадались, што Иван-царевич на сем свете
переглянулись да и замовкли; out of fear of the brothers' threat
не застав уже свайго дарагога работника
пристав к башмашнику, да и таго паслав к царю ... абхадив ён всих мастяров; brides get their wish

phrase: weep that he does not come
note: яны горько плакали, што царевич не приходя
нада была вянчацца. Як сабрались к вянцу
Пазвольте мне, батюшка, пайти самой падарить нищих!
Ён пазволив
Яна пашла и начала дарить да приглядацца
пабачила кольцо, што дала царевичу на том свете, и кольца сястер сваих (бо то быв ён!)
хватила яго за руку, и привяла яго в комнату
Во той, што нас вывяз из таго свету! ... абещали пабить нас, кали мы скажем
Царь на тых сынов рассярдився, наказав их, як сам знав
а после гуляли три свадьбы; closes the story; performer unnamed

phrase: sends for help for the queen
note: король послал по всем царям, по всем городам ... кто бы мог полечить, чтоб королева забеременела?; opens the action
король накормил их досыта, напоил всех допьяна
и начал выспрашивать
Никто не знает ... только взялся крестьянский сын

phrase: gives him gold and three days
note: даёт ему полну горсть червонцев и назначает сроку три дня
Молчи, старая хрычовка, не досаждай мне!
Вот, бабушка, взялся я королю сказать ... да сам не знаю

phrase: tells how the queen will conceive
note: чтоб связали три невода шёлковые ... щука златокрылая ... а королева покушает, тогда и понесёт детище
закинул три невода шёлковые — щука вскочила и порвала все три невода. В другой раз кинул — тож порвала

phrase: ties the nets with his belt
note: снял с себя пояс и с шеи шёлковый платочек, завязал эти невода
закинул в третий раз — и поймал щуку златокрылую

phrase: brings the pike to the king
note: взял и понёс к королю

phrase: has it cooked for the queen
note: Король приказал эту щуку вымыть, вычистить, изжарить и подать королеве
пришла корова, ополощины выпила; she conceives Burya
дорогой оторвала крылышко и попробовала; she conceives the maid's son

performer: the cow, the maid and the queen
note: Все три понесли в один день, в один час: корова, девка-чернавка и королева

performer: the cow, the maid and the queen
note: корова родила человека ... девка-чернавка родила мальчика ... и королева родила сына

phrase: ask leave to walk in town
note: приходят к отцу-королю и просятся в город погулять
Он им позволил ... и дал денег столько, сколько взять смогли
кто бросит выше, тот у нас будет старший

phrase: throws his ball out of sight
note: Буря-богатырь коровий сын так закинул, что из виду пропал
Ну, теперь я над вами старший!
Как так! Коровий сын, а хочет быть старшим!; the dispute leads to the parting
кто этот гад уймёт, тот из нас будет большой!

performer: Ivan-tsarevich and Ivan the maid's son
note: гад пуще разозлился ... тоже ничего не сделал

phrase: quiets the serpent with his cane
note: Буря-богатырь закричал да свою тросточку в воду бросил — гаду как не бывало!
Не хотим быть меньшими братьями!
Ну так оставайтесь сами по себе! — сказал Буря-богатырь и воротился в своё отечество

performer: Ivan-tsarevich and Ivan the maid's son
note: а те два брата пошли — куда глаза глядят
приказал посадить его в крепость; не дают ему ни пить, ни есть трое суток
Богатырь застучал кулаком в каменную стену
захочу — всё кулаком расшибу!
король приходит к нему сам
Никто, окромя меня, не догонит их; они пошли ... в змеиные края
Король начал его просить
взял палицу боевую и меч-кладенец и пошёл

phrase: overtakes his brothers at the bridge
note: догнал братьев близ Чёрного моря у калинового моста ... на столбе написано, что тут выезжают три змея

phrase: orders the hut to turn round
note: Избушка, избушка! Устойся да улягся к лесу задом, а к нам передом

phrase: eat the laid meal and rest
note: Сели, пообедали, потом легли отдохнуть
Кинули — досталось Ивану девкину сыну

phrase: warns him about the dancing jug
note: ты на него не гляди, а возьми наплюй на него, да и разбей
Девкин сын как пришёл, так и уснул
Буря-богатырь, зная, что его братья — люди ненадежные, сам пошёл

phrase: spits on and smashes the jug
note: наплевал-нахаркал на него и разбил на мелкие части
лезет чудо-юда, мосальская губа: змей шестиглавый

phrase: calls his horse and rides out
note: Сивка-бурка, вещая каурка! ... сел на него и поехал на калиновый мост
конь под ним спотыкается ... Есть нам недруг — Буря-богатырь коровий сын
ворона костей моих не занашивала, я сам здесь погуливаю
давай воевать
три головы ему снёс, в другой раз остальные снёс; his widow plots revenge later

phrase: throws the body into the sea
note: Взял туловище, рассёк да и в море бросил

phrase: hides the heads under the bridge
note: головы под калиновый мост спрятал

phrase: ties the horse to his feet
note: а коня привязал к ногам девкину сыну, меч-кладенец положил ему в головы
сам пошёл в избушку и лёг спать
Иван девкин сын проснулся, увидел коня и очень обрадовался
я посмотрел, так господь и коня мне дал!
Буря-богатырь и ему то же сказал об кувшинчике
он на него засмотрелся
и заснул крепким сном
Буря-богатырь, не надеясь на брата, сам пошёл
наплевал-нахаркал на него и разбил вдребезги
давай воевать!
три головы, как кочки, снёс ... а в третий и остальные срубил

phrase: throws body in sea, hides heads
note: туловище, рассёк да в Чёрное море бросил, головы под калиновый мост запрятал

phrase: ties the horse to his feet
note: коня привязал к ногам Ивана-царевича, а меч-кладенец положил ему в головы
сам пошёл в избушку и лёг спать
Утром Иван-царевич проснулся, увидел коня ещё лучше первого
а мне бог коня дал лучше первого
Подходит третья ночь, сбирается Буря-богатырь на караул

phrase: gives his brothers cards and candle
note: поставил стол и свечку ... повесил на него полотенце, дал братьям колоду карт

phrase: tells them to watch for blood
note: как ... с этого полотенца будет в тарелке кровь прибывать, то бегите скорей на мост; they fail to come
он на него наплевал-нахаркал и разбил на мелкие части
Чудо-юда сел на него и поехал; въезжает на мост

phrase: agree not to strike the fallen
note: уговор лучше всего: лежачего не бить; invoked later
и сразу снёс три головы
змей его сшиб
Стой, чудо-юда! Уговор был: лежачего не бить
Чудо-юда дал ему справиться

phrase: fight for hours, Burya cutting heads
note: тот встал — и сразу три головы полетели ... несколько часов возились ... у змея ещё три головы пропали
у богатыря палица лопнула; not an act of a person

phrase: throws his boots at the hut
note: снял с левой ноги сапог, кинул в избушку ... избушка по бревну раскатилася; the ruined hut is found next morning
а братья всё не просыпаются; Burya reproaches them for it
взял обломок палицы, пустил в конюшню ... и выломил из конюшни дверь

phrase: knock the dragon from the saddle
note: жеребцы прибежали на мост и вышибли змея из седла вон

phrase: cuts off the last three heads
note: подбежал к нему и отсёк ему остальные три головы

phrase: throws body in sea, hides heads
note: туловище рассёк да в Чёрное море кинул, а головы под калиновый мост засунул
взял трёх жеребцов, свёл в конюшню
а сам под калиновый мост спрятался
избушка вся рассыпалась, тарелка полна крови
Искали его трое суток — не нашли
Видно, они убили друг друга ... Только что коней оседлали, приготовились было ехать

phrase: comes out from under the bridge
note: Буря-богатырь проснулся и выходит из-под моста
Я вас от смерти избавлял, а вы всё спали
Тут они пали перед ним на колени: — Виноваты

phrase: restores the hut by a spell
note: Пошептал он над избушкою: — Как прежде была, так и ныне будь!
Пообедали и поехали в путь в дорожку
Братцы! Я забыл в избушке плёточку; a pretext to go back

phrase: sends his horse into the meadows
note: пустил его в заповедные луга
Сам оборотился мушкой, полетел в избушку и сел на печку; lets him overhear
пришла туда баба-яга и села в передний угол
сама сделаюсь зелёным лугом ... оборочусь прекрасным садом ... оборочусь старой избушкою; the plans Burya overhears and defeats
Так их, злодеев, и надобно! ... И ты хорошо вздумала

phrase: vows to swallow them as sow
note: оборочусь свиньёю и всех троих проглочу; spoken as a threat; Burya prepares for it

phrase: flies out and becomes a man
note: вылетел на улицу, ударился оземь и сделался опять молодцем
Сивка-бурка, вещая каурка!
навязал на палочку мочалочку
Вот, братцы, без какой плёточки я жить не могу!

phrase: want to rest at the meadow
note: давай лошадей накормим на этой травке и сами отдохнём

phrase: hacks the well, and blood spurts
note: начал этот колодезь сечь и рубить — только кровь брызжет; вдруг ... жара спала; destroys the first widow
Позволь нам сорвать по яблочку
начал сечь и рубить, перерубил все деревья до единого
Братья на него рассердились; leads to their parting at the fork

phrase: want to sleep in the hut
note: давай обночуем в этой хижинке
Сошёл он в эту избушку и начал рубить её — только кровь прыщет!
Поезжай куда хочешь, а мы с тобой не поедем
И поехали они вправо; the sow swallows them
а Буря-богатырь влево

phrase: has the smiths prepare the smithy
note: Обтягивайте кузницу железным листом ... Куйте, кузнецы, двенадцать прутьев железных да накаливайте клещи докрасна!
А вы скажите: ... только высунь язык в кузницу
Кузнецы, кузнецы! Подайте мне виноватого

phrase: tell her to show her tongue
note: только высунь язык в кузницу, мы тебе на язык его и посадим
высунула язык на целую сажень
Буря-богатырь схватил её за язык горячими клещами
До тех пор её колотили, пока рёбра оголились
как ударит её — так все рёбра пополам
Буря-богатырь, пусти мою душеньку на покаяние
Он схватил её за уши; свинья харкнула — и выскочили оба брата и с лошадьми

phrase: dashes the sow against the ground
note: со всего размаху ударил о сырую землю; свинья рассыпалась аредом
Они пали на колени: — Виноваты
Ну, теперь поедемте во путь во дороженьку

phrase: pitch tents in the forbidden meadows
note: раскинули в его заповедных лугах палатки

phrase: sends his first minister to ask
note: призывает к себе первого министра ... узнай, что там за невежи приехали
приехали на королевской дочери свататься ... а коли не отдаст дочери — чтобы высылал войско
Нет, батюшка, я за него идти не хочу; высылайте войско
войско скопилось и отправилось в заповедные луга

undergoer: Ivan-tsarevich and Ivan the maid's son
note: столько выпало войска, что Иван-царевич и Иван девкин сын испугались

phrase: kills the army with his ladle
note: как махнул поварешкою — так половину войска и положил ... и другую половину на месте положил

phrase: spares a one-eyed and blind man
undergoer: the one-eyed and the blind man
note: только оставил одного кривого да другого слепого; they carry his message

phrase: sends them with the same demand
undergoer: the one-eyed and the blind man
note: Доложите ... королю, чтобы выдавал свою дочь Марью-королевну за Ивана-царевича

phrase: agrees and asks for a carriage
note: Делать нечего, надо будет идти за него. Прикажи, батюшка, за ним карету послать

phrase: receives and feasts them with honour
note: король принял их с музыкой ... посадил за столы дубовые

phrase: tells him to let her go
note: а ты скажи: ступай хоть на два!
Позволь мне, Иван-царевич, выйти в другую горницу — переодеться

phrase: flies to the sea as dove
note: оборотилась голубкою и полетела на море
оборотился соколом и полетел за ней следом

phrase: asks her grandfather for three hairs
note: Дай мне, дедушка, с твоей головы три волоска; так я покажу Ивану-царевичу
Дедушка дал ей три волоска
оборотилась голубкой и полетела домой
оборотился такой же девицей
Дедушка, дедушка! Выйди ещё, поговори со мною
Буря-богатырь схватил и сорвал ему голову

phrase: flies back first as an eagle
note: оборотился орлом и прилетел во дворец скорей королевны
На тебе, Иван-царевич, эту голову ... Ты и покажь ей голову

phrase: sets him the riddle of hairs
note: Угадай, царевич, с какого корешка эта травка? Если узнаешь, то пойду за тебя замуж

phrase: slams the head on the table
note: вынул из-под полы голову, ударил об стол: — Вот тебе и корень!
Позволь, Иван-царевич, пойти переодеться в другой горнице
оборотилась голубкою и опять полетела на море
ударил эту голову об крыльцо и говорит: — Где прежде была, там и будь! Голова ... срослась с туловищем; leaves her unsure what happened
Никак твоя голова там была?

phrase: says it was torn off then
note: в те поры, видно, мне и сорвали голову
полетела домой; переоделась ... пришла и села с Иваном-царевичем рядом
На другой день поехали они к венцу закон принять
подаёт ему три прута: один железный, другой медный, а третий оловянный

phrase: takes his place in the bed
note: Коли хочешь быть жив, позволь мне лечь с королевною на твоё место. Царевич согласился

phrase: tries to smother him with pillow
note: наложила королевна на него ногу ... взгребла подушку и начала его душить
взял железный прут и начал её бить; до тех пор бил, пока весь прут изломал

phrase: swears never to do it again
note: Замолилась королевна, великими клятвами заклялась, что не станет этаких дел делать

phrase: tells him his wife is tamed
note: посмотри, как твоя жена у меня выучена; closes the story
Теперь живите благополучно, любите друг друга и меня не забывайте
В одну ночь царю привиделся такой сон: будто у золотого кольца был привязан конь; opens the action

phrase: promises daughter and half the kingdom
note: кто этот сон рассудит и коня того достанет, за того свою дочь отдам и половину царства; answered at the end
думали-думали — никто не может сна растолковать
доложили царю, что у такого-то нищего старичка есть сын Иван; teller unnamed
Царь приказал призвать его. Призвали Ивана
Это не сон, а быль; ... приезжал к тебе двенадцатиглавый змей и хотел царевну украсть
Можно — только тогда, как минет мне пятнадцать лет
царь взял его во дворец, кормил и поил до пятнадцати
Давай, государь, мне коня
как наложит на которую лошадь свою богатырскую руку, та и упадёт
Пусти меня в чистое поле ... Царь его отпустил
три года искал, нигде не мог сыскать
Идет со слезами обратно к царю; his tears draw the old man's question
Что ты, парень, плачешь?

phrase: answers rudely and drives him off
note: Он ему на спрос грубо отвечал, просто-напросто от себя прогнал
Смотри, малый, не помяни меня
Воротился, догнал старика
упал ему в ноги и сказал: — Дедушка, прости меня
нигде не мог сыскать по себе коня

phrase: tells him of a mangy colt
note: от той кобылы народился паршивый жеребёнок; ты возьми его и выкорми: он тебе будет под силу

phrase: lays his hand on the colt
note: наложил на того жеребёнка руку. Жеребёнок нимало не поробил

phrase: takes the colt from the peasant
note: он взял его у крестьянина
покормил несколько времени

phrase: tells the tsar of the horse
note: приехал к царю и рассказал ему, как добыл себе коня
На что мне твоя сила? Я один могу достать
Дал ему царь шесть человек; вот они собрались и поехали
приехали они к огненной реке, через реку мост лежит
раскинули они шатёр ... начали пить, есть, веселиться

phrase: has them keep watch by turns
note: Давайте, ребята, каждую ночь поочерёдно караулить

phrase: each gets drunk and sees nothing
note: всякий напьётся с вечера пьян и ничего не видит; so Ivan watches himself
Наконец пошёл караулить Иван крестьянский сын
едет через реку змей о трёх головах ... есть разве один спорщик ... да и того ворон в пузыре костей не заносил!

phrase: leaps out from under the bridge
note: Иван крестьянский сын из-под моста выскочил: — Врёшь ты! Я здесь
размахнулся своей саблею и срубил змею все три головы
а коня себе взял и привязал у шатра

phrase: kills the six- and nine-headed dragons
note: На другую ночь Иван крестьянский сын убил шестиглавого змея, на третью ночь девятиглавого; their father comes for revenge

phrase: throws them into the fiery river
note: и побросал их в огненную реку
Сейчас выходи ко мне! Зачем побил моих сыновей?

phrase: asks leave to visit his tent
note: Позволь мне наперёд сходить к своему шатру ... — Хорошо, ступай!

phrase: tells them to watch the basin
note: вот вам таз, смотрите в него; когда он полон нальётся крови, приезжайте ко мне
Иван с первого раза срубил у змея четыре головы, а сам по колена в землю ушёл ... наконец одну срубил — по шейку ушёл
посмотрели в таз и увидели, что кровь через край льётся
прибежали и срубили у змея последнюю голову
а Ивана из земли вытащили
Иван крестьянский сын взял змеиного коня и увёл к шатру; not the moon-browed horse, which he already has
а сам оборотился котом
пошёл по мосту через огненную реку, пришёл в тот дом, где змеи жили
и стал дружиться с тамошними кошками
Иван крестьянский сын выслушал всё, что они говорили

phrase: plot to kill him in disguise
note: оборочусь яблоней ... оборочусь колодцем ... сделаюсь кроватью

phrase: says she will swallow them all
note: А я разину пасть свою от земли до неба и всех их пожру!; carried out later as the jaws
вышел из горницы, оборотился человеком
Ну, ребята, сряжайтесь в путь! Собрались, поехали в путь
товарищи Ивановы хотели нарвать яблоков, но Иван не велел

phrase: hacks the apple tree, blood flows
note: начал её рубить; из яблони кровь пошла
Иван увидал колодец, не велел пить
начал его рубить — из колодца кровь потекла
стоит на дороге кровать, Иван и её изрубил

phrase: try to leap the gaping jaws
note: Вздумали с разлёту через пасть скакать. Никто не мог перескочить; только перескочил один Иван
вынес его из беды чудесный конь

performer: a tiny man with seven-verst whiskers
note: Отдай мне коня

phrase: threatens to take it by force
note: а коли не отдашь честью, то насилкой возьму!
Отойди от меня, проклятый гад, покудова тебя конём не раздавил!
сшиб его наземь
сел на коня и уехал
Входит Иван в избёнку и сильно о коне тужит

phrase: tells how his limbs were eaten
performer: a man with no arms or legs
note: он у меня и руки и ноги отъел! ... за то, что я у него на столе хлеб поел!

phrase: asks how to regain the horse
note: Иван начал спрашивать, как бы назад коня достать?
сними перевоз, три года перевози, ни с кого денег не бери

phrase: runs the ferry three years unpaid
note: пошёл на реку, снял перевоз и целых три года перевозил безденежно
они дают ему денег, он не берет
он не берет ... — По обещанию
Скажи, добрый молодец, почему ты денег не берёшь?
У меня ехидный человек коня отбил

phrase: offer to get his horse back
